descs.t: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a localized ceasefire in Oleshky, a front line city in southern Ukraine hit by a food crisis, in a deal the White House says was brokered by First Lady Melania Trump. Reuters reports the pause is meant to let humanitarian aid in and civilians out. We go through what was agreed, what Russia has announced for the Kherson region, and what could still go wrong.

A ceasefire limited to one Ukrainian city, Oleshky, is now agreed, with the White House crediting Melania Trump for brokering it. The deal is meant to open the way for aid and evacuations in a city facing a food crisis. We look at whether Russia will keep its word, why critics doubted the deal, and what it could mean for wider talks to end the war.

Critics online said Melania Trump could never negotiate a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. Then Reuters reported both sides had agreed to one in Oleshky, a trapped southern city hit by a food crisis. We break down the deal, the people it could save, and why Russia's record means the world should watch closely.
